Hi Helen —

Appreciate the clear list. I've pulled together a concise phase-level deployment plan and checklist (attached). High-level summary below — happy to iterate in a short call.

Phase A — Discovery & Pre-reqs (1–2 weeks)
- Kickoff workshop (stakeholders: IT, Security, App owners)
- Deliverables: network diagram, required firewall rules, VPC/subnet CIDR agreement, KMS provisioning plan
- Redwood tasks: provide test endpoints, initial IAM roles, onboarding guide

Phase B — Integration & Pilot (2–3 weeks)
- Establish VPC peering or PrivateLink, test end-to-end requests, validate DN/SSL certs
- Pilot: 1–2 customer app instances routed to Redwood test environment
- Deliverable: integration runbook + signed checklist

Phase C — Canary & Performance Validation (2 weeks)
- Canary rollout across 3 waves: 1% traffic (48 hrs), 10% (72 hrs), 25% (72 hrs)
- KPIs: 95th/99th latency, error rate, token cost per 1k tokens variance, model output quality for sample prompts
- Rollback triggers: sustained error rate >1% over 30 mins, 99th-latency >2x SLO for 15 mins, quality regression on evaluated prompts

Phase D — Cutover & Parallel Run (1 week)
- Gradual shift to Redwood Dedicated endpoints; parallel routing for 48 hrs; final DNS cutover and traffic acceleration
- Post-cutover validation script run and escalation list

Phase E — Stabilization & Handover (2 weeks)
- 24/7 on-call for first 72 hours; weekly ops review; handover to Starnet ops with runbook and dashboards

Estimated total: 8–10 weeks from kickoff to stabilized production (typical for medium complexity integrations).

Security & Audit notes:
- We retain request and audit logs for 90 days by default in hosted; Dedicated/Private options support customer-controlled retention and KMS for encryption at rest.
- SOC 2 summary attached; we can provide scoped evidence for Prod/Preprod on request.

Attachments: Redwood_Implementation_Plan_v1.pdf, Implementation_Phase_Checklist.xlsx, SOC2-summary.pdf

Next steps: if this aligns, let's book a 60-min technical workshop (we recommend this week or early next). Priyom will take the lead on the implementation project plan and Rishi will own capacity/throughput validation.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Couple of implementation notes to include in the checklist:

1) Dedicated capacity sizing — recommend starting with a committed pool sized for 1.5x observed peak during pilot traffic. This gives headroom for autoscale warm-up.

2) Canary sizing & automation — we should automate canary ramp using traffic-split policies with automatic rollback. Proposed thresholds (repeat): 1% / 10% / 25% over ~7 days total for cautious customers, but for Starnet (SLA-focused) I'd recommend compressing to 1% (48h) -> 10% (48h) -> 25% (48h) if monitoring passes.

3) KV cache warm-up — if customers rely on long context sessions, include a cache-warm step in the Pilot to avoid cold-start latency spikes. Priyom, please add the KV pre-warm script to the checklist.

4) Observability — ensure token-level latency and cost dashboards are provisioned in the console before Canary. Monica, add a Grafana dashboard link to the runbook.

Rishi

Hi Helen — quick answers and next steps: 

1) SOC2 evidence: the attached SOC2-summary.pdf outlines retention and logging for Hosted and Dedicated. For Dedicated we can provide customer-facing reports showing audit logs; for Private (on-prem) we fully hand over logs to customer control.
